after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s),\,-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s),\,-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)⟩,\,0\le s<\sqrt{2}\pi .
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)\cdot \sqrt{2},\,-\frac{1}{2}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s))\cdot \sqrt{2},\,-\frac{1}{2}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s))\cdot \sqrt{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s),\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s),\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s))⟩ \\  & =⟨(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s))\cdot \sqrt{2},\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)\cdot \sqrt{2},\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)\cdot \sqrt{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{2}s),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

   

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2}s)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2}s)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2}s)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2{sin}^{2}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)+2{cos}^{2}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)} \\  & =\sqrt{2({sin}^{2}⁡(\sqrt{2}s)+{cos}^{2}⁡(\sqrt{2}s))} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

r′(s)=⟨dds(22sin⁡(2s)),dds(−12cos⁡(2s)),dds(−12cos⁡(2s))⟩=⟨22cos⁡(2s)⋅2,−12(−sin⁡(2s))⋅2,−12(−sin⁡(2s))⋅2⟩=⟨cos⁡(2s),22sin⁡(2s),22sin⁡(2s)⟩r″(s)=⟨dds(cos⁡(2s)),dds(22sin⁡(2s)),dds(22sin⁡(2s))⟩=⟨(−sin⁡(2s))⋅2,22⋅cos⁡(2s)⋅2,22⋅cos⁡(2s)⋅2⟩=⟨−2sin⁡(2s),cos⁡(2s),cos⁡(2s)⟩

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=⟨\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{4}){cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =1 \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{3{sin}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+4{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)=⟨\,\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,t⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
Let $T(t)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter $t.$ Since we are given the curve $r(t)$ parametrized by the parameter $t$ (not the arc length $s$), we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9({cos}^{2}⁡(3t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(3t))+1} \\  & =\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨-9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,-9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\sqrt{(9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)^{2}+(-9\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\sqrt{{9}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡3t+{cos}^{2}⁡3t)} \\  & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\,\frac{9}{\sqrt{10}}\,}{\sqrt{10}}=\frac{9}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}),\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})⟩,\,0\le s<6\pi .
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))⟩ \\  & =⟨-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\cdot \frac{1}{3},\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\cdot \frac{1}{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3}),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3})⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\cdot \frac{1}{3},\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\cdot \frac{1}{3}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}),\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =|\frac{1}{3}|\sqrt{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{3})+{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{3})} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)=⟨-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,t⟩$ for $0\le t\le \frac{\pi }{4}$
after.worked_solution:
Let $T(t)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter $t.$ Since we are given the curve $r(t)$ parametrized by the parameter $t$ (not the arc length $s$), we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(\operatorname{tan}⁡t)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{tan}^{2}⁡t+1} \\  & =\sqrt{{sec}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$
